Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to
address City Council, please complete a speaker card and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. City Council will hear public
comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote and on matters not listed on the
agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for
consideration at a future City Council meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council: Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less
and
directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or
other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are
available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the
agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48
hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements
can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has
been posted will also be made available for public inspection. Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City
Clerk’s Department, during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every
other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

departmental workspace safety improvements, Room 15 is being redesigned to create a more

office furniture including cubicles and storage cabinets.

Municipal Code §15.44.060, and require consensus of the entire City Council. Any
Councilmember may nominate an individual who falls into one of the two categories:

SUBJECT: AWARD OF CONTRACT – CONTINUED ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT
  CONSULTING SERVICES

Background:

In December 2022, City Council awarded a new contract to Kosmont Companies (Kosmont) for
economic development consulting services for a three-year term. Kosmont offers a full range of
professional economic development services, including but not limited to, business recruitment
and retention activities, strategic planning, marketing, proforma analysis, maintaining and
updating databases, and evaluating infrastructure funding strategies. Kosmont has worked
extensively with the City since 2018 and has a strong understanding of local market trends and
added value to the analysis of current projects. They provided a detailed work plan to achieve
the objectives of the City’s economic development goals.

Kosmont has provided a variety of economic development and real estate advisory services to
the City including broad-based analyses, such as producing a quarterly market dashboard
observing market changes in various land use typologies between the City and surrounding
communities; and project-specific analyses, such as performing a net fiscal impact analysis for
residential reuse of the former California Youth Authority site, conducting market due diligence
for the proposed development at the Norwalk Entertainment District, and provided an economic
analysis for the upcoming Heart of Norwalk Specific Plan.

Additionally, during the current three-year period Kosmont prepared an update to the 2018
Economic Development Opportunities Plan (Plan) in 2023 that identifies nodes throughout the
City that could promote economic development. The Plan analyzed retail/office/commercial
voids, demographics, shopping patterns, traffic counts, daytime population statistics, and most
importantly identified ten Economic Nodes/Strategic Areas for focused economic development
and planning efforts. Kosmont also developed quarterly market reports for the City commonly
known as Market Dashboards. Kosmont prepared a feasibility analysis of an Enhanced

SUBJECT: HEART OF NORWALK SPECIFIC PLAN UPDATE

Background:

On July 6, 2021, City Council adopted The Heart of Norwalk Vision Plan for the future of San
Antonio Village and the Firestone Corridor, two key neighborhoods in the center of the City. The
Plan was developed in partnership with the City, the Southern California Association of
Governments (SCAG) and the consulting firm, The Arroyo Group (TAG). This Vision Plan sets
the overall tone for how the study area can grow in both the commercial and housing sectors,
while balancing place making and open spaces. The Vision Plan emphasizes providing new
commercial amenities, open spaces, complete streets, and affordable housing to support
Norwalk residents. In order to implement this vision, staff initiated the drafting of a Specific Plan
that will establish zoning regulations and development standards to make this vision into reality.

Discussion

The proposed Heart of Norwalk Specific Plan (“Specific Plan”) effort intends to establish zoning
regulations that will permit housing and desired commercial uses while ensuring that each
development contributes to community goals. It will also establish a program of street, open
space, and infrastructure projects to support the vision of the plan and future growth and propose
funding and implementation measures needed to implement the proposed Specific Plan.

The Heart of Norwalk Specific Plan area contains a wide variety of commercial and residential
zoning districts. Staff notes that currently within the commercially zoned properties, housing is
permitted in conjunction with a commercial development (mixed use) with an approved
Conditional Use Permit. It is estimated that these commercial sites could reasonably be
developed with 2,053 residential units under current zoning regulations. The Specific Plan is
intended to be implemented over a 30-year period.

Heart of Norwalk Specific Plan Update  Page No. 2

Additionally, the development of the Specific Plan will help the City in meeting its Regional
Housing Needs Allocation (RHNA) of 5,034 units. The current Housing Element accounted for
many of the sites within the Heart of Norwalk area as residential inventory sites available for
development. Therefore, the Housing Element contains a program that commits to adopting the
Heart of Norwalk Specific Plan, which would allow residential use.

Community Feedback

The project team has received robust and consistent input for the project since the beginning of
the Vision Plan process in fall 2020. The Vision Plan outreach campaign engaged approximately
5,300 residents between December 2020 and March 2021. Nearly 100 residents attended four
online events that were held in February and March 2021, 363 surveys were completed by
community members, and over 3,000 residents engaged with Heart of Norwalk social media
content.

Outreach in the Specific Plan process consisted of virtual and in-person community workshops
and participation at three Front Street events in the summer of 2022 and in the summer of 2024.
Further community workshops and social media engagement will take place prior to the adoption
of the Specific Plan.

Throughout the outreach process, members of the public have consistently expressed the desire
for high-quality local commercial options, places to enjoy in groups and spend time in public.
They desire an authentic center to the City, with local and national businesses, places to walk
and spend time, nightlife, and spaces that can encourage and celebrate local culture, such as
performance arts spaces.

Front Street, a focal area for businesses and nightlife, retains its historic feel by preserving older
buildings. It caters to the community’s younger population. Norwalk Town Square, on the other
hand, offers shopping, family entertainment, and convenient parking. Multifamily residential uses
are also supported, as they contribute to the desired commercial amenities. Public surveys and
workshops revealed a desire to connect these districts through streets, prioritizing walking, biking
and public space over traffic movement.

On February 20, 2024, a Study Session was conducted with City Council to provide an update
of the Heart of Norwalk Specific Plan and gather feedback from Council and the public.

Specific Plan Progress

The project team circulated the Draft Environmental Impact Report (DEIR) on June 23, 2025, for
a 45-day public review period ending on August 7, 2025. Concurrently, the draft Specific Plan is
also available for public review for the same duration. Although not required, staff plans to
conduct meetings with property owners within the area of the Specific Plan in July 2025. These
meetings aim to provide property owners with a refresher on the Specific Plan and address any
concerns. The City will continue to receive public feedback and additional input regarding the
proposed land use plan to finalize the Specific Plan’s zoning regulations and DEIR.

Once the review period concludes, staff will commence preparing the associated Response to

Staff anticipate scheduling the Specific Plan and the EIR for consideration to the Planning

November 2025. The Arroyo Group will be providing a presentation of the draft Specific Plan
during the July 1, 2025, City Council meeting.
